Bob folds a piece of paper, then punches a hole into the paper and unfolds it again. The unfolded paper then looks like this:
<image1>
Along which dotted line has Bob folded the paper beforehand?
<image2>

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The paper unfolded above is a square; there are four round holes on the paper, arranged in a 2×2 symmetrical pattern of two columns left and right and two rows up and down. Among the options below, A is two diagonal crease lines, B is three vertical crease lines, C is one vertical center line and one horizontal center line, D is multiple oblique parallel crease lines, and E is two vertical crease lines. Reasoning: If the paper is folded first and then one hole is punched, after unfolding, the positions of the holes will be mirror images with respect to the fold line. The four holes in the figure are symmetrical both left-right with respect to the vertical center line and up-down with respect to the horizontal center line, so one vertical center fold line and one horizontal center fold line are needed. Option C exactly represents these two center fold lines.

method.method_draft: Read the unfolded paper in the image: there are four holes arranged as a 2x2 symmetric grid, with the left-right positions matching and the top-bottom positions matching. From the text, Bob folded the paper before punching one hole, then unfolded it. Use the folding rule that holes on the folded stack mirror across each fold line when unfolded. A 2x2 hole pattern indicates two perpendicular folds, one vertical and one horizontal through the center, so the correct dotted-line label is C.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a paper with four resulting holes, which means the punch went through four layers after folding. Since one punch produced four holes, Bob must have folded the paper twice so that the punch location was duplicated into four positions when unfolded. Among the answer choices, only C shows two fold lines crossing at right angles through the middle, which is the only option consistent with a two-fold stack producing four holes.
